input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement sits at our preferred position. § 2.1 (p0012) expressly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and that Customer pays only for Services ordered in an executed Order Form, with a decision not to order further being neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any unstated minimum-use charge, and § 12.3 (p0050), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "take or pay", "volume", and "prepaid" surfaced no take-or-pay or volume-cap mechanic; the only "shortfall" references (§§ 22.2–22.3) concern audited underpayment, not a purchase commitment. The exclusivity language in § 2.2 restricts sourcing rather than imposing a purchase or volume commitment, so it is addressed under the exclusivity rule and is not flagged twice here. No redline required.
